standard_prerequisites: Context span 2112-2164: over a field k of characteristic 0 the projection f: X = Spec(k[t, x_1, x_2, ..., y_1, y_2, ...]) -> Spec(k[x_1, x_2, ..., y_1, y_2, ...]) = Y is of finite presentation; Z is the closed subset cut out by x_1 (t - 1) = 0, x_2 (t - 1)(t - 2) = 0, x_3 (t - 1)(t - 2)(t - 3) = 0, ...; U = union of the opens U_j where y_j (t - 1)...(t - j) is nonzero; on each U_j the image f(Z cap U_j) is the set of points where x_1, ..., x_j are zero and y_j is nonzero

Context claim and proof: B = f(Z cap U) = union_j f(Z cap U_j) is not a finite union of locally closed subsets of Y; the induction on n shows any cover B = A_1 union ... union A_m has m >= n for all n (the closure of B is (x_1 = 0), some A_i is open in (x_1 = 0) but cannot contain a point with y_1 = 0 since for points of B y_1 = 0 forces x_2 = 0; the right shift map x_i -> x_{i+1}, y_i -> y_{i+1} identifies B with B cap (y_1 = 0))

Chevalley's theorem (Algebra, theorem-chevalley; Morphisms, section-constructible) gives constructibility of images of constructible sets under finitely presented morphisms - the positive backdrop stated in the section preamble
core_obligations: The context provides f: X -> Y of finite presentation between affine schemes
T = Z cap U is a locally closed subset of X
f(T) = B is not a finite union of locally closed subsets of Y by the complete context induction
Hence the image of a locally closed subset under a finitely presented morphism of affine schemes need not be a finite union of locally closed subsets
proof_roadmap: Instantiate the context morphism, closed subset and open
Take T = Z cap U locally closed with image B
Conclude by the context induction that B is not a finite union of locally closed subsets
